# Config reference

Generated by `conductor-docs`. The keys, their types, the rules and the type descriptions are the specification's, [`spec/domains/config.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/spec/domains/config.yaml); each default is what `conductor config show` prints for a file that leaves the key out, read through the same library the binary runs. A key marked required is one whose absence `conductor config validate` refuses. The hand-written [config guide](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/docs/config.md) says which part of conductor reads each key.

> The one file conductord reconciles from, `conductor.config/2`, read from `--config`, else the `conductor-config` setting, else ~/.b10x/conductor/conductor.yaml. It holds the `daemon` section (its port, TLS listener, reconcile cadence, the one store URL, the secrets source, the dashboard's served path and its operators), `globals` (the defaults every instance starts from) and `instances[]`. An instance is one organization conductor runs: its placement, where its repositories come from, where their checkouts are, where conductor keeps its records, state and cache, which kind and model each role runs on, its cadence, thresholds, reports, and who decides each decision class; every key an instance or a role writes overrides the global one. Precedence is role over instance over global (`Level`), and `EffectiveSettings` shows every key with its effective value and the level it came from. These types hold the effective config, after defaults; the file may leave out every key of an instance but its name, its sources and its checkouts. No field takes a secret: the file names one as `secret:<name>` (`conductor.secret.SecretName`). The config is desired state and is not kept in the store (§ 8); every change through `PutConfig` is validated, written, committed with its actor and reason, recorded as `ConfigChanged` and reconciled. A `conductor.config/1` file is read once by `conductor config migrate`.

## Top level

The file, `conductor.config/2` (design architecture-next § 9). A key it does not declare is an error, and so is a value that looks like a token. A value under a secret-bearing key (one whose name ends in `token`, `password`, `secret` or `bearer`, and the password of a `daemon.store` URL) is `secret:<name>` and nothing else. `daemon` is conductord's own section, `globals` the defaults every instance starts from, `instances` the instances it reconciles. `default` is the instance a command runs when neither `--instance` nor the `conductor-instance` setting names one; it names an instance of the file. No two instances share a `session_prefix`, and at most one has none; no two share a `state` or a `records` directory. The host registry that checked this across config files is gone (§ 11): one daemon reads one file. `instances` holds at least one instance, unless `daemon.kubernetes` is set: a daemon that runs its instances as pods starts with none, and a consumer control plane adds each (`AddInstance`). Where it is set, every instance's name is a `KubernetesName` of at most 39 characters, so that `conductor-instance-<name>-data` is at most 63.

| Key | Type | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | required | `version == "conductor.config/2"` |
| `daemon` | [Daemon](#daemon) | each key its own | `defined(daemon.kubernetes)` or `instances.count >= 1`; `not defined(daemon.kubernetes)` or every `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name.count <= 39` |
| `globals` | [Globals](#globals) | each key its own |  |
| `default` | [InstanceName](#instancename) | none | `not defined(default)` or some `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name == default` |
| `instances` | list of [Instance](#instance) | required | `defined(daemon.kubernetes)` or `instances.count >= 1`; `not defined(daemon.kubernetes)` or every `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name.count <= 39`; `instance.name` distinct across `instances`; `instance.session_prefix` distinct across `instances`; `instance.state` distinct across `instances`; `instance.records` distinct across `instances`; `not defined(default)` or some `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name == default` |

## Daemon

The `daemon` section (design architecture-next § 4, § 5.2, § 8, § 9): `port`, the loopback port of the global API on 127.0.0.1, 1 to 65535, absent 7300; `tls`, the TLS listener, absent when none is configured; `cadence.reconcile`; `store`, the one URL of the deployment's shared database, which the daemon hands to every instance runtime it starts; `secrets`, the secrets source; `dashboard`, the path the daemon serves the dashboard app at, absent `/`; `operators`, the deployment's operators, at least the one the Unix user names on a single host; `upgrade_timeout`, how long an upgraded instance runtime has to answer before the daemon rolls it back to its previous binary, a duration, absent 120 s; `timeout`, how long an instance has to answer one federated read of the global API before it is a row with `state: unreachable`, a duration, absent 5 s. `loopback`, whether the daemon serves the loopback listener on `port`, absent true: a box with no local operator writes false, its API then the TLS listener alone, so false with no `tls` is refused at validate by the key's YAML path, and `daemon serve --install` writes a system unit for it rather than the user unit. `substrate_slots`, the size of the local substrate daemon's model-token slot pool, absent 0 (substrate 0.20.0, design 11: a slot is daemon configuration, never a per-request value): the operator declares `--secret-slot model_token_<i>=<daemon dir>/slots/model_token_<i>` for each `i` below it; before a box opens the daemon writes the instance's `model_token` into a free slot's file (mode 0600), names that slot in the start, and frees it when the box closes. `unattended`, whether `daemon serve` at its start does for each instance of the file what `conductor setup --apply` does, each only where it is missing: writes and commits its records skeleton, trusts its checkouts and records directory, and activates its checkouts root as a `worktree` workspace; a skeleton whose repository has no commit yet is committed as it lies. The listeners answer while it seeds, `/readyz` `503` meanwhile, and `503` for as long as the process runs once a step failed. Absent false, and the start then creates none of them. `address`, the address the listener on `port` binds, an IP address, absent `127.0.0.1`: on a loopback address the listener answers a `Host` naming that address beside `127.0.0.1` and `localhost`; one that is not loopback lets a probe or a published port of a container reach the daemon, and every `/v1/` request on it then carries an Identity bearer, as on the TLS listener; the probes and the metrics answer without one. `kubernetes`, the instance pods (`conductor.config.Kubernetes`), absent none. `control_token`, written `secret:<name>`, names the control token: a request on either listener whose bearer equals that secret's value, read from the secrets source and never from the file, is admitted as the machine principal `control-plane` (`conductor.operator.ActorKind` `ControlPlane`), with or without `tls`, for the reads of `/v1/` a person may make and for `POST /v1/instances`, `PUT` and `DELETE /v1/instances/{name}` and `POST /v1/instances/{name}/restart`, and nothing else. Absent, no request is admitted so, and the daemon answers as it did before the key existed.

The `globals` section (design architecture-next § 9, § 10): the defaults every instance starts from, each overridden by an instance key of the same name and by a role's own key. `roles` are the built-in and custom roles with their kind, model and profile; the host roles `supervisor` and `teacher`, which the daemon starts, are written here only (a `conductor.config/1` file's `host.roles` becomes `globals.roles` at `config migrate`). `tuning` is the tuning grant, empty by default (`conductor.improvement.TuningGrant`, § 13 row 7).

## Instance

One instance, `instances[]` of the file (design architecture-next § 9: name, `placement`, sources, checkouts, records, roles, overrides of any global key). A path is written absolute or under `~`, which is the home directory; the effective path is absolute. `operator` is how sessions name the person who decides class O. `placement` names the placement the instance's box is opened at (`conductor.placement`, § 6). `session_prefix` is the prefix of every session the instance starts. It is required: `config validate` refuses an instance that writes none, naming the prefix `conductor config migrate` would write (`SuggestedPrefix`). For one release a file without it still loads, so that a running instance keeps working until the operator migrates it: its sessions keep the bare names `conductor`, `conductor-dev` and `<repository>`. `conductor` is derived: the conductor that serves the instance.

The overrides: `roles`, `limits`, `controllers`, `cadence`, `thresholds`, `retention` and `usage` are the keys `globals` holds for every instance (`Globals`); each one an instance writes overrides the global value, key by key, and a role's own key overrides both (precedence role over instance over global, `Level`). These keys are kept as they were before v1; what is new is that an absent one takes the global value before conductor's built-in default. `limits` are the instance's box as a whole, the cpu, memory and task limits every role of the instance runs inside (they move here from `confinement.limits`).

A key path written `a[].b` is the key `b` of each element of the list `a`. A default that holds `<name>` holds the instance's name.

| `usage.watcher` | string | none |  |
| `usage.rotate` | string | none |  |
| `operator` | string | none |  |
| `catalog` | [Catalog](#catalog) | none |  |
| `catalog.repository` | string | required |  |
| `catalog.path` | string | required |  |
| `catalog.names` | `plain` \| `hex` | `plain` |  |
| `secret_syncs` | list of [SecretSync](#secretsync) | `[]` |  |
| `secret_syncs[].name` | string | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].source.repository` | string | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].source.branch` | string | `main` |  |
| `secret_syncs[].source.path` | string | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].secrets` | list of [ForgeSecret](#forgesecret) | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].secrets[].owner` | string | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].secrets[].repository` | string | none |  |
| `secret_syncs[].secrets[].name` | string | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].command` | string | required |  |
| `secret_syncs[].dry_run` | string | none |  |
| `gates_policy` | string | none |  |
| `model_token` | [SecretName](#secretname) | none |  |
| `forge_token` | [SecretName](#secretname) | none |  |
| `forge.route` | `gates` \| `direct` | `gates` |  |
| `conductor.served_by` | [InstanceName](#instancename) | derived |  |
| `conductor.session_name` | [SessionName](#sessionname) | derived |  |

## Types

### InstanceName

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.InstanceName`.

### Harness

The file writes a harness in lower case: `claude` or `codex`.

One of `claude` | `codex`. Specified as `conductor.config.Harness`.

### Tokens

A count of tokens. The file writes a whole number, or thousands with `k`: `300k`.

Written as integer. Specified as `conductor.config.Tokens`.

### Gibibytes

A size in GiB (2^30 bytes). The file writes a whole number with `G`: `15G`.

Written as integer. Specified as `conductor.config.Gibibytes`.

### TimeOfDay

A time of day, UTC, `HH:MM`.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.TimeOfDay`.

### Source

Where an instance's repositories come from. The file writes `{github: <owner>}`, `{local: <path>}` or `{gitlab: <group or root>}`; a `local` or `gitlab` source may add `exclude: [<path under the root>]`, and a `gitlab` source `host: <host name>`.

A repository is the directory that holds `.git` at depth 1 or 2 under a root (`<root>/<repo>` or `<root>/<group>/<repo>`), named by its path under the root (`<group>/<repo>`); the root is a `local` source's path, and for the checkouts of the other sources `checkouts.root`. A repository whose name is an `exclude` entry, or lies under one, is not listed and not placed. Absent, `exclude` is empty. A `github` source takes no `exclude`: GitHub lists its owner's repositories, and the collectors that read that list do not filter it.

One of the forms the keys table lists. Specified as `conductor.config.Source`.

### GitHubSource

An owner on GitHub, whose repositories are the instance's.

Keys: `owner`. Specified as `conductor.config.GitHubSource`.

### LocalSource

A directory whose repositories are the instance's.

Keys: `path`, `exclude`. Specified as `conductor.config.LocalSource`.

### GitLabSource

A group (or the root) on a GitLab forge, whose repositories are the instance's. `host` is the forge's host name, without a scheme or a path, such as `gitlab.example.com` for a self-hosted GitLab; absent, it is `gitlab.com`. The collectors read that forge with `glab api --hostname <host>`: one repository row and one specification row per checkout of a project of the group and its subgroups, and one per project without a checkout, archived ones included. A project's checkout is each git checkout under `checkouts.root` whose `origin` remote is on the host and names the project, read from its git config with no network read. A checkout is the repository, named as every repository is, by its path under `checkouts.root`, whatever its project is called: the workspace file, the snapshots, `repository activity`, the charters and the dispatches name it so, and the project's id and path are used only where the forge is called. Two checkouts of one project are two repositories. A project without a checkout is named by its path under the group, the path its checkout would have under the root; one whose name a checkout of another project holds fails the snapshot, which names both. A project two `gitlab` sources list, as sources whose groups nest do, is one repository, which the source written first records. A checkout under a directory that is no repository name is not recorded and stops no snapshot; the collecting command names it on standard error. An `exclude` entry names a checked-out project in either form: by its checkout's path under the root, which leaves that checkout out, its project then not listed under its own name either; or by the project's path under the group, which leaves the project out with every checkout of it.

Keys: `group`, `host`, `exclude`. Specified as `conductor.config.GitLabSource`.

### Checkouts

The directory holding the instance's checkouts, and the one holding their managed worktrees.

Keys: `root`, `trees`. Specified as `conductor.config.Checkouts`.

### CatalogNames

How a catalog entry's file stem spells a repository's name. The file writes it in lower case: `plain`, the name itself, or `hex`, the lower-case hex of the name's UTF-8 bytes.

One of `plain` | `hex`. Specified as `conductor.config.CatalogNames`.

### Catalog

The instance's catalog: `repository` names a repository whose checkout lies under `checkouts.root`, written as its path under the root; `path` is a directory on that repository's `origin/main`, written relative to its top, whose `.json` files name the cataloged repositories, one file each, the name being the file's stem as `names` spells it. Absent, `names` is `plain`. An instance without a catalog records no catalog membership.

Keys: `repository`, `path`, `names`. Specified as `conductor.config.Catalog`.

### CommandWord

A value a start command passes to the harness as one shell word, unquoted: a role's model, agent, settings file or profile file. Letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `:`, `/`, `-` only, so that no shell reads it as more than that word.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.CommandWord`.

### SessionPrefix

The prefix every session one instance starts carries: letters, digits and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Session names are one namespace for the whole machine, so no two instances of the file share a prefix, no prefix starts with another followed by `-`, which would let one session name carry both, and no prefix followed by `-` begins a name an instance without a prefix keeps, such as `conductor-dev`.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.SessionPrefix`.

### SessionName

A harness session name on this machine: `<session_prefix>-<role or repository>`, or without a prefix the role or the repository itself. A repository nested as `<group>/<repo>` is written `<group>-<repo>` in it, as in the workspace, since a session name is one path word.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.SessionName`.

### Role

The harness and model one session role runs on, such as `director` or `lead` (`conductor.config.RoleName`, or its old name, as the file writes it); the harness agent the role starts with, such as `repo-controller`; the settings file it starts with; and the profile file its session starts with through `--append-system-prompt-file`, in place of the agent and of the text the binary carries for the role, read at start. The settings and profile files are written absolute or under `~`. Absent, a role names no agent, no settings file and no profile. `session_name` is derived, never chosen: the name the role's session starts under, `<session_prefix>-<role>`, or `<role>` when the instance has no prefix, `<role>` as the file writes it; absent for `lead` (`controller`), whose sessions are named per repository, `<session_prefix>-<repository>` or `<repository>`. The file may leave it out, and may write only that value. An instance whose file writes no `roles` has the three roles `director`, `maintainer` and `lead`, each on `claude` with the model `opus`, written for this release under their old names `conductor`, `conductor-dev` and `controller`, which the start tasks and the watch's context lines select them by; they move to the new names with the tasks, so that no running instance's sessions are renamed. Without a profile or an agent, a role the binary carries a profile for (`maintainer`, `supervisor`, `teacher`, `controller`) starts from that text, which the `claude-code` kind writes into the agent's state, and `director` with the agent `conductor`. In v1 the maintainer is retired and the host's file `host.yaml` is gone: the host roles are `globals.roles` (`Globals`, design architecture-next § 9, § 11). `read_only_tools` names the tools, beyond the guard's built-in read-only allowlist, that the guard allows the role's sessions without a rule of its own, such as a read-only MCP tool; every other tool outside the guard's ruled set is denied. A tool with a rule of its own (Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, SendMessage, Bash, Monitor) is decided by that rule whatever this list says. Absent, it is empty. A `lead` (`controller`) role the file writes that names an `agent` names a `profile` as well: a session the `systemd` provider starts passes `--setting-sources project,local`, which loads no user-level agent (the `none` provider adds `user` for `claude --bg`), so a controller starts only from a profile, never from its agent; a controller role with an agent and no profile is refused by its `profile` path. One with neither is valid, as the built-in role is. `limits`, `writable` and `network` are the envelope each session of the role asks for: the limits of one session, the places it may write, and its network; a box that cannot be set up is a refusal with substrate's reason and nothing falls back (`conductor.placement`, design architecture-next § 6). A role's limit lies at or under the instance's limit of the same key, where the instance sets one, since every session of the instance runs inside the instance's box. Absent, a role sets no limit, writes its default places, and has the network open. The request leaves out three things on purpose: the readable paths, since the box binds the root read-only and nothing narrower is planned; the programs a session may run, since a program list belongs to the tool server; and a lifetime, since sessions are long-lived and conductor ends them. `forge_token_env` names the environment variables, such as `GH_TOKEN` or `GITLAB_TOKEN`, that carry the forge tokens a session of the role may use: each a name of capital letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. It is carried on the session request a provider receives (`conductor.session.SessionRequest`); the variables' values are never part of the config. Absent, it is empty. `grant` is what each session of the role may call through `tool` (`conductor.tool.RoleGrant`): its verbs, the repositories and paths they read, the most bytes one answer carries and the grant's time to live. Absent, the role's default tools that exist as verbs: `show`, `search` and `diff`, over the whole working directory, 65536 bytes per answer, for the session's life. A settings file pins its instance: its `env.CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE` is the instance's name, and each of its hook commands that runs `conductor` names the instance first, `CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE=<name> conductor guard …`, since the harness does not pass the environment its starter set on to a session it forks. A role's own settings file that pins no instance (no `env.CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE`, or a hook command that runs `conductor` without the prefix), as the binary's do, starts pinned: `session start` and `spawn` write its content with the pin set to `<state>/sessions/<session name>.settings.json` and start the session with that copy, and `config validate` reports it, by its `settings` path, as a note. A settings file that pins another instance, or cannot be read as JSON, is a problem `config validate` names by its `settings` path, and `session start` and `spawn` refuse it (`InstanceNotPinned`). A role that names none starts with its default written pinned (`conductor.session.SessionStartRefusal`).

`kind` (design architecture-next § 7, § 9: "roles with kind, model and profile") is the agent kind that fills the role's slot; absent, `claude-code`, the only kind in v1. The same role written under `globals.roles` is the default of every instance; one an instance writes under its `roles` overrides it key by key (precedence role over instance over global, `Level`).

`token_owner` names the operator whose Claude token from the instance's pool the role's agent leases, so a controller started for Remote Control appears in that owner's Claude app. A controller's key only: on any other role it is a problem. Absent, the pool's lease rule applies (the token with the most headroom). A named owner with no Available token refuses the start (`NoTokenAvailable`); no other owner's token is taken.

Keys: `role`, `kind`, `harness`, `model`, `agent`, `settings`, `profile`, `session_name`, `read_only_tools`, `limits`, `writable`, `network`, `forge_token_env`, `grant`, `token_owner`. Specified as `conductor.config.Role`.

### Limits

The CPU, memory and process limits of a box, as systemd sets them on a cgroup: `memory_max` its `MemoryMax`, in GiB, written as a size, `15G`; `cpu_weight` its `CPUWeight`, from 1 to 10000; `tasks_max` its `TasksMax`, the most processes and threads at once. Absent, a key sets no limit.

Keys: `memory_max`, `cpu_weight`, `tasks_max`. Specified as `conductor.config.Limits`.

### Writable

One place a role's sessions may write: a path written absolute or under `~`, made absolute, or one of the words for a place resolved per session when it starts: `checkout`, the checkout the session starts in (a controller's repository's, conductor-dev's this repository's); `trees`, the managed worktrees of that checkout under `checkouts.trees`; `build-cache`, the build tools' caches under the home directory (cargo's among them); `scratch`, the session's scratch, under `$TMPDIR` and, for a controller, `<cache>/scratch/<repo>`, under the instance's own `cache` (`<repo>` its repository, `/` written `-`); `harness-state`, the harness's own state directory, `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`; `records`, the instance's records directory. Absent, a role writes `checkout`, `trees`, `build-cache`, `scratch` and `harness-state`, and the `conductor` role `records` as well; a list the file writes takes their place.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.Writable`.

### Network

A session's network. The file writes it in lower case: `open`, the host's network, the only one there is.

One of `open`. Specified as `conductor.config.Network`.

### RepoCache

Whether `conductor build run` gives a cargo-based command its repository's compile cache. The file writes it in lower case: `on` or `off`.

One of `on` | `off`. Specified as `conductor.config.RepoCache`.

### ConductorSession

The conductor a session of the instance messages: its own, `session_name` being its director role's, `<session_prefix>-<role>` or `<role>` with the role as the file writes it (`<session_prefix>-conductor` for the old name), when the instance names a `director` (`conductor`) role; else the conductor of the file's `default` instance, which serves it, `served_by` naming that instance; neither when no conductor serves it. Derived, never chosen: a file may leave it out, and may write only that value.

Keys: `served_by`, `session_name`. Specified as `conductor.config.ConductorSession`.

### Controllers

How many controllers of the instance work at once, at most, how many sub-agents one controller runs at once, at most, and how many pull requests of one repository may wait for review before conductor sends that repository no new dispatch, `0` meaning no limit. Absent, they are 5, 4 and 3.

Keys: `max_working`, `max_subagents`, `max_open_reviews`. Specified as `conductor.config.Controllers`.

### RepositoryRule

What the instance holds true of the repository whose name `match` names: its activity, and whether it ships without releases. The file writes an activity in lower case: `active` or `inactive`. `no_releases` is the reason the repository ships without releases (docs published on merge, a specification consumed at `main`); a repository it marks is left out of every K5 reading of `metric compute`, which names it as skipped once. A rule writes at least one of the two.

Keys: `match`, `activity`, `no_releases`. Specified as `conductor.config.RepositoryRule`.

### Cadence

How often conductor runs a cycle, when its daily cycle starts, and how often the watch reads the sessions and main's CI. The file writes a duration as a whole number with `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`: `2h`, `180s`.

Keys: `cycle`, `daily`, `watch`, `ci`. Specified as `conductor.config.Cadence`.

### Thresholds

Conductor's context above which it hands over; the filesystem whose free space the disk thresholds read, written absolute or under `~`; free disk under which the watch reports it, from which a further fall is reported again, under which no session starts, and under which a full gate takes a build slot; the size above which a build is expected to write enough to ask for a slot; free disk under which the full-gate watchdog stops the gate's process group and from which it resumes it; how often the watchdog reads it; and how long a live controller session, and every one of its sub-agents, may write nothing to its transcript before the watch reports it silent, a duration as `cadence` writes one; and how many CPU cores `conductor build run` leaves to the desktop; and how many `conductor build run` commands run at once on the host, every instance's together: a request is granted only while fewer disk grants than this are `Granted` or `Running`, waits in the queue's order while they are not, and is never refused for it, 0 for no bound. A command's job count, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and `MAKEFLAGS=-j`, is its share of the cores: the cores less the reserve, over the build slots (all of them at 0), at least 1; a `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` in the environment above that share is lowered to it, and one line says so. Then whether `build run` gives a cargo-based command its repository's compile cache, one sccache server and directory per repository that all of its worktrees share, and that cache's size; and the short lane: how many build slots besides `build_slots` admit only a command the ledger knows to be short, 0 turning the lane off, and the longest p90 run time of such a command, a duration as `cadence` writes one. A request is short when the ledger holds at least 3 earlier runs of its repository and command in 14 days whose p90 run time is at most `short_lane_max`, and no short-lane run of it outlived twice that in the last 24 hours; a short-lane run's job count is its share, at most 4. Then how long a live driven session may make no progress, neither a report conductor received nor a commit in its checkout or any of its trees, before the watch reports it stalled, and how long a host grant may stay `Requested` before the watch reports the build queued, each a duration as `cadence` writes one. Then how long a managed tree that is dirty or unmerged may be untouched before reclaim removes its `target/` and lists it stale, kept, a duration as `cadence` writes one. Absent, the filesystem is `/`, the silence 30 minutes, the reserve 2 cores, the build slots 3, the repository cache `on` and its size 2G, the short-lane slots 1 and their longest p90 3 minutes, the stall 45 minutes, the queued build 30 minutes and the staleness 48 hours. Whether `build run` gives a cargo-based command line-table-only debug information, `lean_debuginfo`: `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG` set to `line-tables-only`, each unless the environment sets it or the workspace manifest sets that profile's `debug`; absent, true.

Keys: `context_handover`, `disk_path`, `disk_low`, `disk_clear`, `disk_admit`, `build_slot`, `build_size`, `gate_stop`, `gate_resume`, `watchdog_every`, `silent_session`, `cpu_reserve`, `build_slots`, `repo_cache`, `repo_cache_size`, `lean_debuginfo`, `short_lane_slots`, `short_lane_max`, `stalled_session`, `build_queued`, `tree_stale`. Specified as `conductor.config.Thresholds`.

### Retention

How many snapshots' observations the instance keeps: those of the newest `snapshots` complete ones. Absent, it is 12, a day at the 2-hour cadence.

Keys: `snapshots`. Specified as `conductor.config.Retention`.

### Report

Where a report goes, as whom it is posted, and on which occasions.

Keys: `channel`, `as`, `when`. Specified as `conductor.config.Report`.

### Authority

Who decides a class-C and a class-O decision. The file writes `conductor` or `operator`.

Keys: `class_c`, `class_o`. Specified as `conductor.config.Authority`.

### SecretSync

One secret sync of the instance: a file on a branch of one of its repositories that the organization's own tool publishes into GitHub Actions secrets, which its CI reads. `name` names the sync on the board; `source` is the file; `secrets` are the secrets it feeds, one or more; `command` is the command line that publishes it, and `dry_run`, when given, the one that shows what `command` would publish without publishing it. Conductor runs neither: the snapshot reads the source's last commit and each secret's `updated_at`, and the board flags `secret stale: <name>` when the source changed after a secret was written. The conductor session runs `command` only where the instance's `rules.md` grants it. No two syncs of an instance share a name.

Keys: `name`, `source`, `secrets`, `command`, `dry_run`. Specified as `conductor.config.SecretSync`.

### SecretSource

The file a secret sync publishes: `repository` names a repository whose checkout lies under `checkouts.root`, written as its path under the root; `path` is the file, written relative to that repository's top; `branch` is the branch its last commit is read on, as `origin/<branch>`, `main` when absent. Neither path takes `.` or `..` steps.

Keys: `repository`, `branch`, `path`. Specified as `conductor.config.SecretSource`.

### ForgeSecret

One GitHub Actions secret a sync feeds, by its `name`: the organization `owner`'s secret, or, when `repository` is given, that repository's of the owner. It is read with `gh api` (`GET /orgs/<owner>/actions/secrets/<name>`, `GET /repos/<owner>/<repository>/actions/secrets/ <name>`), which answers the secret's `updated_at` and never its value.

Keys: `owner`, `repository`, `name`. Specified as `conductor.config.ForgeSecret`.

### Usage

How the instance reads its harness accounts' usage. `probe` is a command, run with `sh -c` on each snapshot, that prints the accounts as one JSON object: `accounts`, a list, each with `id` (the account; conductor keeps nothing else of it, never an e-mail address or a name), `active` (whether it is the account in use), `health` (`exhausted` for one with nothing left) and `usage.windows`, a list of `{name, used_percent, resets_at}`; every other key is ignored. `watcher` is the systemd user unit that rotates the accounts, which `conductor doctor` reports running or not. With `probe` set, the watch resumes a session whose tmux pane stands on the `Usage limit reached · …` banner once the probe shows the active account with headroom. `rotate` is a command, run with `sh -c`, that makes an account with headroom the active one: with it set, the watch resumes such a pane once any account has headroom, and runs `rotate` once first. `rotate` is valid only beside `probe`. Conductor names no tool: all three are the operator's. Absent, none is set: no probe runs, doctor reports no watcher and the watch resumes no pane.

Keys: `probe`, `watcher`, `rotate`. Specified as `conductor.config.Usage`.

### ForgeRoute

The route the instance's forge writes take. The file writes it in lower case. `gates`: through the bot route `b10x-gates`; the guard leaves `gh` and `glab` reading only, and `conductor run` commits and pushes the records with `b10x-gates bot`. `direct`: with the forge's own CLI and git; the guard lets a session open, update, comment on and merge (auto-merge included) the pull or merge requests of its own repository with `gh pr` or `glab mr`, the repository named with `-R`/`--repo`, and `conductor run` commits and pushes the records with plain git. Under either, every other forge write (another repository's, a credential's, an API write) is denied as before.

One of `gates` | `direct`. Specified as `conductor.config.ForgeRoute`.

### Forge

How the instance writes to its forge: the `route`. Absent, it is `gates`.

Keys: `route`. Specified as `conductor.config.Forge`.

### PlacementName

Stand-in for `conductor.placement.PlacementName`, which the placement unit declares (design architecture-next § 6). Declared here only so that this branch validates on its own; the coordinator replaces every use with `conductor.placement.PlacementName` and removes this type.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.PlacementName`.

### OperatorGrant

Stand-in for `conductor.operator.Grant`, which the operator unit declares: what an operator may do (design architecture-next § 3 row `conductor.operator`: answer decisions, change settings, start, stop and upgrade instances, purge, join). Declared here only so that this branch validates on its own; the coordinator replaces every use with `conductor.operator.Grant` and removes this type. The file writes a grant in kebab case: `answer-decisions`.

One of `answerdecisions` | `changesettings` | `startinstances` | `stopinstances` | `upgradeinstances` | `purge` | `join`. Specified as `conductor.config.OperatorGrant`.

### OperatorRole

An operator's role in the config (design architecture-next § 5.3: "the daemon records them as an operator of that instance with the grants the config gives their role"), such as `owner` or `reader`; the config names its own roles.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.OperatorRole`.

### DaemonOperator

One operator of the deployment, `daemon.operators[]` (design architecture-next § 5.3, "Several operators"): the Identity principal's name (on a single host with no Identity, the Unix user), their role and the grants they hold. A grant belongs to a human only; an agent actor holds none (§ 3, Actors).

Keys: `name`, `role`, `grants`. Specified as `conductor.config.DaemonOperator`.

### TlsListener

The daemon's TLS listener (design architecture-next § 4, § 5.2): the address and port it listens on, written `<host>:<port>`, for a dashboard deployed elsewhere and for every client of a daemon on a remote box; every request presents an Identity bearer.

Keys: `listen`, `cert`, `key`, `identity`. Specified as `conductor.config.TlsListener`.

### SecretsSource

Where the daemon resolves the `secret:<name>` values the file names (design architecture-next § 9, decision 6): `keychain`, the OS keychain on the control host (`secrets-keychain`), or `remote`, the Secrets service where conductord runs in a deployment (`secrets-remote`). `namespace` is the secrets namespace the names live in; `url` is the Secrets service's address, for `remote` only.

Keys: `source`, `namespace`, `url`, `dir`. Specified as `conductor.config.SecretsSource`.

### DaemonCadence

The daemon's cadence (design architecture-next § 4): how often it reconciles when nothing else triggers a pass, a duration as `cadence` writes one. Absent, 60 s.

Keys: `reconcile`. Specified as `conductor.config.DaemonCadence`.

### KubernetesName

A name Kubernetes takes as a DNS label (RFC 1123) and as a label value: lower-case letters, digits and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or a digit, at most 63 characters. A namespace and the owner of `daemon.kubernetes` are written so. So is the name of an instance the daemon runs in a pod, since its pod and its Secret are named `conductor-instance-<name>` and its volume claim `conductor-instance-<name>-data`: the longest affix is 24 characters, so such an instance's name is at most 39 (the invariant of `Config`). `config validate` refuses a name that breaks either rule, naming its YAML path.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.KubernetesName`.

### KubernetesVolume

The volume claim of each instance pod (`conductor-instance-<name>-data`), which holds its checkouts, worktrees, records, state, cache and its own sqlite store: `size`, its request, written as a size, `20G`, and required; `storage_class`, the storage class it names, absent the namespace's default class. A retired instance's claim is kept.

Keys: `size`, `storage_class`. Specified as `conductor.config.KubernetesVolume`.

### KubernetesQuantities

Quantities of one resource list of a pod's container, each written as Kubernetes writes a quantity (`500m`, `2`, `512Mi`, `4Gi`) and passed through unchanged; absent, the list sets none, and the namespace's LimitRange applies.

Keys: `cpu`, `memory`. Specified as `conductor.config.KubernetesQuantities`.

### KubernetesResources

The requests and the limits of each instance pod's container. Absent, both are empty. They are not `limits` of the instance (`conductor.config.Limits`, a box's cgroup), which a pod-run instance does not read.

Keys: `requests`, `limits`. Specified as `conductor.config.KubernetesResources`.

### KubernetesEnv

One environment variable of each instance pod's container: `name`, capital letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit; and either `value`, the text itself, or `secret`, written `secret:<name>`, a secret the daemon resolves from its secrets source (`daemon.secrets`), never from the file. Exactly one of the two is written. The daemon writes each value into the instance's Secret (`conductor-instance-<name>`) and the container reads it by `secretKeyRef`, so no value stands in the pod's spec. It carries what an instance pod needs from outside, such as `GH_TOKEN` or `GITLAB_TOKEN` for the forge's CLI, the `GIT_AUTHOR_*` and `GIT_COMMITTER_*` identity, or `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` and `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`; which forge token a pod gets is the operator's decision, not conductor's, and an instance's `forge_token` takes the place of the entry of its forge's variable in its own pod. A name conductor sets for the pod itself is refused at validate, naming its YAML path (`daemon.kubernetes.env[<i>].name`): `HOME`, `PATH`, and every name that starts with `CONDUCTOR_` (among them `CONDUCTOR_CONFIG`, `CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE`, `CONDUCTOR_STORE`, `CONDUCTOR_API_TOKEN`, `CONDUCTOR_API_LISTEN` and `CONDUCTOR_CONFIG_SOURCE`); the invariants of `Kubernetes` say so.

Keys: `name`, `value`, `secret`. Specified as `conductor.config.KubernetesEnv`.

### Kubernetes

The daemon runs each instance's runtime as its own pod (design: instance pods, the direct route), beside the systemd unit and the child process; it is a supervisor, not a placement and not a sandbox, so `placement` stays what it is and a placement that opens a box is refused at validate beside this key, naming its YAML path. The daemon reaches the Kubernetes API with its mounted service account and creates, per instance, a Secret `conductor-instance-<name>` (the instance's config file as the daemon renders it, the runtime's API token, the model token and every `env` value), a volume claim `conductor-instance-<name>-data`, and a pod `conductor-instance-<name>` that runs `image` with `conductor --config <data>/conductor.yaml instance serve`, restart policy `Never` (the daemon restarts it), the `restricted` pod security fields, and no service account token. Each of the three carries the labels `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=conductord`, `app.kubernetes.io/component=instance-runtime`, `conductor/daemon=<owner>` and `conductor/instance=<name>`; the daemon adopts and cleans up by the first three. The daemon builds the pod, its Secret and its claim from this key and the instance's name alone: nothing an instance's mapping holds reaches the image, the command, a volume, an env source, a service account, a host path, the namespace, a label or an annotation, and a `secret:<name>` in a mapping resolves against the daemon's secrets source only, never a Kubernetes Secret by name. `namespace`: the namespace of the instance pods, the daemon's own or another one. `image`: the image every instance pod runs, `<repository>:<tag>`; a changed image restarts each instance pod on it. `owner`: the value of `conductor/daemon`, which tells one daemon's pods from another's in one namespace. `api_port`: the TCP port the runtime serves its API on in its pod, which the daemon proxies `/v1/instances/{name}/…` to, 1 to 65535. `volume`, `resources` and `env` as their types say. Absent, the daemon runs no pod: every runtime is a systemd unit or a child process, as before. Where this key is set, the file may hold no instance (`instances: []`): every instance arrives through `AddInstance`. Without it, a file with no instance is refused by its path `instances`. `namespace`, `image`, `owner`, `api_port` and `volume.size` are required and have no default.

Keys: `namespace`, `image`, `owner`, `api_port`, `volume`, `resources`, `env`. Specified as `conductor.config.Kubernetes`.

### StoreUrl

The one URL of the deployment's store: `sqlite:<path>` or `postgres://…`, its password a `secret:<name>`.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.store.StoreUrl`.

### Source

Where a secret's value is kept: `Keychain`, the `secrets-keychain` backend (the OS keychain: the Secret Service on Linux, the native keychain on macOS), on the control host; `Remote`, the `secrets-remote` backend (the Secrets service: encrypted, tenant-scoped custody), where conductord runs in a deployment. `secrets-federation` routes each namespace to one of them (§ 9). `Files`: a directory of mounted files, one file per secret, the file's name the secret's name, its content the value with one trailing line end dropped: the shape a cluster's secret volume has. Conductor reads it and never writes there; a put into it is refused with `SourceReadOnly`.

One of `keychain` | `remote` | `files`. Specified as `conductor.secret.Source`.

### OperatorName

An operator's name: the Identity principal, or the Unix user on a single host with no Identity.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.operator.OperatorName`.

### SecretName

What the config names after `secret:` (`forge_token: secret:gitlab-bot` names `gitlab-bot`).

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.secret.SecretName`.

### AgentKindName

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.agent.AgentKindName`.

### RoleGrant

A role's grant as the config file writes it (`instances[].roles[].grant`): the verbs its sessions may call; the repositories and the paths they may read, each path relative to the session's working directory (empty: the whole working directory); the most bytes one answer may carry; and the time to live of a session's grant from its start (absent: the session's life). Absent, a role is granted its default tools of design § 3 that exist as verbs: `show`, `search` and `diff` for every role, over its whole working directory, at most 65536 bytes per answer, for the session's life.

Keys: `tools`, `repositories`, `paths`, `max_output_bytes`, `ttl`. Specified as `conductor.tool.RoleGrant`.

### Verb

The verbs of the read group (design § 6.3). The file and the wire write them in lower case: `show <path> [--lines a:b | --fn <symbol>] [--max n]` prints a bounded range of one file, and `unchanged since <time>` for a re-read, in the same session, of a range whose content has not changed; `search <pattern> [--path p]` prints the lines that hold the pattern, as text, under the grant's paths; `diff [--stat]` prints the checkout's uncommitted change, as a stat by default. The build group: `test [<package>] [--filter f]`, `check [<package>]` (clippy over every target, warnings denied) and `fmt [<package>]`. Version control: `commit -m <message> -- <paths>`. Team: `send <role-or-name> <text>` and `report <status> <line>`. Later stories add the other groups.

One of `show` | `search` | `diff` | `test` | `check` | `fmt` | `commit` | `send` | `report`. Specified as `conductor.tool.Verb`.

### TuningGrant

The tuning grant (design architecture-next § 3 row `conductor.improvement`, § 9, § 13 row 7): the keys the tuner may change, each with its bounded range. Empty by default: the tuner proposes, the brief shows the proposals, and the operator writes keys into the grant. A tuner proposal is applied only through `conductor.config.PutConfig`, and only when its key is one of the grant's and its value lies inside that key's range; otherwise `PutConfig` refuses the agent (`ActorNotHuman`).

A struct, not an entity: the grant is desired state, so it lives in the config (§ 8: "config is desired state and is not kept in the store"), at `globals.tuning` (`conductor.config.Globals`), and changes only as the config does, through `PutConfig` by a human actor, with a `ConfigRevision` recording who and why. No proposal type exists in this domain to carry it. The grant never names a key under `tuning`, so an agent never widens its own grant.

Keys: `keys`. Specified as `conductor.improvement.TuningGrant`.

### TunableKey

One key the tuner may change, and the range it may change it within (design architecture-next § 9, § 13 row 7): `path` is the key's YAML path as `config show --effective` names it (`thresholds.silent_session`, `cadence.watch`), `min` and `max` the bounds, both inclusive.

Keys: `path`, `min`, `max`. Specified as `conductor.improvement.TunableKey`.

### RemoteDaemon

A substrate daemon on a remote host or cluster, `substrate-daemon --tcp-listen --tcp-bearer-file`, reached over HTTPS/WSS at `url` with an Identity bearer (§ 6, `placement.daemon: <url>`). The bearer is a secret the config names and never holds (§ 9). `trust_roots` is the PEM file of the roots the daemon's certificate is verified against and `server_identity` the DNS name it must carry: substrate 0.20.0's SDK has no ambient roots and takes both explicitly; `server_identity` written absent is the URL's host.

Keys: `url`, `bearer`, `trust_roots`, `server_identity`. Specified as `conductor.placement.RemoteDaemon`.

### Activity

One of `active` | `inactive`. Specified as `conductor.direction.Activity`.

### Decider

One of `conductor` | `operator`. Specified as `conductor.decision.Decider`.
